subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Annie Dillard's memoir An American Childhood. In the text, the author discusses her family's evening routine.

Every night after dinner, we would gather in the living room to read together. We read even during the warmer months, when we could have been outside on the porch. Reading aloud was our way of saying we belonged to each other, we had created our own world, we were complete.

©1987 by Annie Dillard
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It summarizes the information that came before it in the text.
choices.B: It illustrates that reading together provides meaning beyond the simple act of sharing stories.
choices.C: It explains that the family prefers to stay indoors during warm weather.
choices.D: It suggests that the author feels equally connected to her family whether they read together or not.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately describes how the underlined portion functions in the text as a whole. The first two sentences of the text establish that the family gathered nightly to read together year-round. The underlined portion then indicates that reading together didn't merely provide entertainment: it also represented "belonging to each other" and feeling "complete." The underlined portion thus illustrates that reading together provides meaning beyond the simple act of sharing stories.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. Although the text's second sentence mentions that they read "even during the warmer months, when we could have been outside," this detail isn't the focus of the underlined portion. Instead, the underlined portion indicates that reading together served purposes beyond simple entertainment: to create a sense of belonging and completeness.
